A colossal pillared throne-hall carved from living black granite, rows of immense rune-stamped columns marching away into glowing gloom, the vaulted ceiling lost in smoke and shadow far, far above.
A vast forge-cavern split by rivers of channeled molten lava, great stone furnaces roaring along every wall, orange light flickering across centuries of carved and blackened stone.
A grand hall flanked by colossal carved statues of ancient dwarf-kings, each a hundred feet tall, hewn from the mountain's living heart, their bearded faces receding into absolute shadow.
A deep mine-shaft plunging through tier after tier of glowing rock, iron scaffolding spiraling downward into luminous dark, the bottom utterly invisible, warm air rising from unknown depths below.

A cathedral-vast hall of precise geometric stonework, every surface cut to interlocking angles of impossible complexity, the ceiling a vaulted lattice of carved stone ribs arching hundreds of feet overhead.

A great underground market-cavern spanning half a mile of rough-hewn floor, hundreds of stone stalls crowding beneath stalactite columns, lantern-light spilling across the cacophonous, smoke-thickened air.
A bridge of ancient black iron spanning a bottomless chasm, the far wall invisible in darkness, wind moaning upward from depths unknown, the bridge itself wide enough for ten dwarves abreast.
A treasure-vault of staggering scale, gold and gemstone piled in drifts against walls a quarter-mile apart, the heaped wealth glittering under the cold blue flame of eternal rune-lanterns.
A flooded lower deep where black water fills vast carved chambers, stone causeways threading between submerged pillars, bioluminescent fungus lighting the still surface with pale green fire below.

A furnace-hall of roaring industrial scale, dozens of enormous forges thundering along both walls simultaneously, the heat pressing like a physical weight, sparks cascading in glittering curtains to the stone floor.

A rune-carved gate-hall of immense fortification, the great iron doors themselves thirty feet thick, every surface dense with glowing inscription, the hall behind stretching back into layered defensive darkness.

A stalactite cavern where an entire dwarven city has been built into the hanging stone, dwellings and workshops clinging to formations hundreds of feet long, connected by rope bridges and iron ladders.

A vast library-hall cut into pale limestone, shelf upon carved shelf rising fifty feet on every wall, iron reading-galleries bolted across the stacks, ten thousand years of stone-pressed records filling the silence.
A great bathhouse carved into a geothermal cave, scalding mineral springs filling tiered stone pools across an enormous floor, steam rising to a ceiling lost entirely in billowing white vapor above.

A hall of ancestor crypts receding for what seems like miles, stone sarcophagi stacked floor to ceiling in carved alcoves, rune-lanterns burning dim amber along the unending processional corridor of the dead.

A vast mushroom-farm cavern, enormous fungal growths rising thirty feet from a carefully irrigated floor, the ceiling dripping with moisture, blue and white bioluminescence replacing all need for fire or lantern.
A coliseum-scale training hall hewn from red sandstone, tiered viewing galleries rising along every wall, the practice floor below scarred by ten thousand years of axe and hammer, vast and roaring.
A grand aqueduct-hall where carved stone channels carry underground rivers along elevated stone arches for hundreds of yards, the water roaring in the silence of an enormous excavated natural cave.
A council chamber of severe scale, a single circular table of black granite forty feet across at the center, the domed ceiling above bearing the carved history of the hold in obsessive detail.

A smelting-cavern of titanic industrial purpose, ore descending by iron chute from shafts above into furnaces the size of houses, slag running in glowing streams toward collection trenches far below the walkways.
A hall of maps carved directly into a vast flat stone floor, the relief topography of the entire underground realm cut to precise scale, spanning two hundred feet of navigational stone cartography.
A vast brewery-cavern beneath the hold, enormous stone vats the size of cottages arrayed across the floor, the smell of hops and fermentation filling every corner of the amber-lit underground space.

A collapsed deep hall partially reclaimed by underground jungle, phosphorescent vines threading ancient carved columns, roots splitting geometric stonework, the original ceiling shattered open to a shaft of cold mineral dark above.
A grand observatory-shaft bored straight up through a thousand feet of mountain to a single pinhole of sky, the circular walls carved with astronomical charts, the floor set with a brass orrery.
A war-hall of arms and banners stretching the length of a city block underground, racks of weapons rising to the carved ceiling, captured enemy standards draped across pillars of ancient black stone.
